question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle ownership model become a supported core doctor surface after the prerequisite stack and non-mutating read contract are complete?
rationale: The PR adds a new core lifecycle capability from an open RFC; an environment gate and strong tests do not establish permanent product ownership, support expectations, or the acceptable SQLite observation contract.

options.title: Sponsor core diagnostics
options.body: Accept the core direction after the WAL/SHM defect, prerequisite contract, upgrade proof, and real-behavior evidence are complete.

options.title: Evaluate the full stack first
options.body: Keep this slice open but unlanded until maintainers review the prerequisite and dependent Claws lifecycle PRs as one product direction.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Close the implementation stack if Claws ownership and reconciliation should not become a supported core capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core diagnostics
recommendation.body: Accept the core direction after the WAL/SHM defect, prerequisite contract, upgrade proof, and real-behavior evidence are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of shared-state and doctor architecture makes Peter the best available decision owner for both product placement and the SQLite observation contract.
